item.title: Jewish Political Activism in the United States
item.description: A long-run survey of Jewish political activism in the United States from 1880 to 2025, tracking shifts from immigrant labor organizing to civil-rights coalition politics, pro- and anti-communist foreign-policy networks, and contemporary campus/digital-era polarization. Emphasizes mechanisms of influence (votes, unions, litigation, philanthropy, lobbying, media) while separating documented influence from conspiratorial tropes.

item.title: Jewish Political Activism in the United States (1880--2025)
item.description: Historical synthesis of Jewish American political activism (1880–2025): labor unions, civil rights, foreign policy and Israel debates, organizational density, and modern digital-era advocacy—plus how myths of “Jewish influence” diverge from measurable channels.
